sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F145][F8].

The path was a step change rather than a smooth climb: revenue jumped 22.3% in FY2022 to $23.0 billion, then fell 5.2% in FY2024 to $23.5 billion before rebounding 9.8% in FY2025 [D131][F5][D201][F7][D236][F8].
The FY2024 decline came from lower storm cost recovery revenues of roughly $1,090 million and lower fuel cost recovery revenues of roughly $526 million [P34].
Operating margin swung from a 15.5% low in FY2021 to a 41.3% high in FY2023, a 25.8pp range that dwarfs the revenue cycle [F20][F22].
FPL remains the anchor, at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue, and contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% growth that year [D271][D273][D236].
FPL's FY2025 revenue rose $1,243 million on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan cost recovery revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery revenues [P21].
Operating income grew 9.9% a year against 7.7% for revenue, and in FY2025 operating costs grew 0.2pp faster than revenue, at 10.0% [F146][F145][D257][D249].
Net income compounded at only 0.4% a year and diluted EPS fell 0.7% a year, so per-share results lagged the top line badly [F147][F149].
FY2025 net income fell $111 million, or $0.07 per diluted share, on lower Corporate and Other results, partly offset by higher FPL and NEER results [P28].
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sat 1.8pp above the 30.3% window median and well above the 15.5% FY2021 low [F24][D300][D298].
The FY2025 bridge was flat, with operating margin up just 0.3pp while D&A ran at 25.5% of revenue [D247][D224].
D&A rose $951 million in FY2025 mainly on higher amortization of deferred storm costs from Hurricanes Debby, Helene and Milton, partly offset by reserve amortization [P16].
In FY2025 net margin of 26.5% sat 5.6pp below the 32.1% operating margin, as other expense of $3.75 billion and a -17.7% effective tax rate pulled the two apart [F40][F24][D327][X64][D226].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $12.5 billion covered net income 1.83 times, in line with the 1.95x window median [F64][F32][D227][D319].
Operating cash flow was 48.4% of revenue, and investing outflow of $23.9 billion dwarfed it, so free cash flow was deeply negative [D225][F72].
Capital intensity is the reason: D&A alone ran at 25.5% of revenue in FY2025, and stock-based compensation was a negligible 1.5% of operating cash flow [D224][D228].
The swing from a net over-recovery to a net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by roughly $89 million in FY2025 [P19].
Total debt reached $95.0 billion in FY2025 against $2.81 billion of cash, leaving net debt of $92.2 billion [D230][D229][D231].

Net debt has risen every year of the window, from $34.3 billion in FY2018, and net cash of -357.4% of revenue ranks at the 0th percentile against a -235.4% peer median (n=3) [D9][D231][D232][D328][D329].
The current ratio of 0.60x is the window high but still below 1.0x, with working capital of -$9.23 billion [F128][D305][F120].
Free cash flow was negative, so the $4.68 billion of dividends and $23.4 billion of debt issued funded the build-out, and the diluted share count rose 0.6% in FY2025 [D233][X90][D251].
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x in FY2025 at 0.60x, a one-period flag [R1][F128].
For a regulated utility this reflects routine short-term debt rollover rather than a liquidity crisis, but it leaves little cushion if refinancing conditions tighten [R1].
Net debt rose for a seventh straight year to $92.2 billion in FY2025, a medium-severity flag [R2][D231].
Debt is compounding faster than equity, so the balance sheet is increasingly the constraint on the growth model rather than the growth itself [R2].
The effective tax rate moved -23.3pp in FY2025 to -17.7%, a low-severity flag [R4][D226][D191].
The negative rate reflects clean energy tax credits at NEER rather than an error, but it makes net income hard to read against operating profit [R4][P11].
Whether FY2026 operating margin holds above the 30.3% window median or slips toward the 15.5% FY2021 low, in the FY2026 10-K [D300][D298].
Whether net cash of -357.4% of revenue in FY2025 moves further below that level or improves toward the -235.4% peer median, in the FY2026 10-K [D232][D329].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers toward the 1.95x window median from 1.83x in FY2025, in the FY2026 10-K [D319][D227].
